sources.title: Technical Discipline: Flight Deck Human Factors
sources.license_note: Public FAA guidance summarized; linked documents remain authoritative
mechanisms_absorbed: flight deck HMI is a certification-oriented human-factors discipline
automation alerting workload complexity fatigue and design-related error are coupled concerns

sources.title: AC 20-175 — Controls for Flight Deck Systems
sources.license_note: Public FAA document; operational/certification context must be checked for each project
mechanisms_absorbed: flight-deck control devices require human-factors evaluation
traditional and multifunction controls must be assessed in operational context

sources.title: AC 25.1302-1 — Installed Systems and Equipment for Use by the Flightcrew
sources.license_note: Public FAA document summarized rather than reproduced
mechanisms_absorbed: design should minimize design-related flightcrew errors
remaining errors should be detectable and manageable by flightcrew

sources.title: ISO/FDIS 9241-130 Ergonomics of human-system interaction — User assistance within interactive systems
sources.status: Final Draft International Standard under development; approval phase in 2026
sources.license_note: Paywalled draft; only public status/abstract synthesized; never treated as a released conformance requirement
mechanisms_absorbed: user assistance is a distinct cross-platform HCI concern
assistance selection usage and dependencies require explicit design

sources.title: IEC 80601-2-78:2019+AMD1:2024 — Medical robots for rehabilitation, assessment, compensation or alleviation
sources.status: Published International Standard consolidated version; amendment publication 2024-03-12; stability date 2028
sources.license_note: Paywalled IEC standard; only public product metadata and scope synthesized
mechanisms_absorbed: rehabilitation robots that physically interact with patients require basic-safety and essential-performance treatment
user-facing rehabilitation-robot UI composes medical safety, robotics, accessibility and physical/multisensory interaction rather than requiring a duplicate UI owner
